messages:
OpsBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool node failure detected for customer 'Sunnyside Health' (dedicated-pool-id: dp-7f2b). Node gpu-node-17 reported unresponsive NVidia driver and hit kernel oops. Incident severity: P2. thread created at 1782006789
Sara (oncall): i'm on it. paging s-rep oncall. can you confirm impact to running jobs?
Mike SRE: seeing repeated `GPU H/W ECC` errors in dmesg on gpu-node-17. NVLink flaps, processes failing with CUDA error 999.
Alex M: which tenant(s) are on that node? customer is on dedicated pool so likely isolated but need to confirm if any shared control-plane tasks affected.
Lee Infra: dp-7f2b layout: nodes 16-20 are dedicated; Sunnyside has pinned tasks across 16-18. Looks like 17 hosts 2 serving pods for Sunnyside's model 'sunnyside-ggml-v2' (replicas=2).
Julia (solutions): Victoria, FYI — CSM pinged. Sunnyside's SLAs expect 5ms median, they were surface-level when load hit.
Victoria CSM: copying customer PM and infra lead. They reported intermittent 503s ~ 5m ago. asking if we have fallback.
Ben (prod): OpsBot, what does the automated remediation suggest?
OpsBot: Auto-remediation: cordon/drain candidate node and reschedule pods to healthy nodes in pool. Suggested action: manual drain + live migration to fallback pool (if capacity). No automated fallback to hosted for dedicated customers without opt-in.
Sara (oncall): i will cordon and drain gpu-node-17 now. running `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
Mike SRE: hold on — draining will evict memory-resident KV cache for that model. we should snapshot caches or restart replicas in new node to avoid cold-start latency. recommend spinning up replacement pod(s) on 16 and 18 before evict.
Alex M: agree. i'll trigger scale-up for sunnyside-ggml-v2 to replicas=4 with nodeSelector for pool dp-7f2b so K8s can place them on 16/18 and any spare nodes.
Julia (solutions): communicate to the customer that we will do a rolling eviction and might see brief spikes in latency. i'll draft a message.
Victoria CSM: pls add estimated ETA for full restoration. they want an update in 10 min.
Sara (oncall): scale command sent: `kubectl -n sunnyside set replicas deployment/sunnyside-ggml-v2 4`. watching pod status... pod sunnyside-ggml-v2-5 Pending -> Running on gpu-node-16 :thumbsup:
Mike SRE: two new pods running on node-16 and node-18. starting traffic shift via routing weight adjustments in the control plane.
Ben (prod): lowering traffic to node-17 at edge: `rbac route-weight sunnyside:0.1->gpu-node-17` then gradually 0.
OpsBot: NOTE: node 17 has ongoing I/O errors on NVMe as well; replacement likely required. Node flagged for hardware replacement ticket hw-replace-7782.
Sara (oncall): ok starting drain now. `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — evicting 2 pods.
Mike SRE: eviction completed, pod termination logs show CUDA error 999 then graceful shutdown. KV cache persisted to S3: `s3://redwood-cache/sunnyside/replica-17-snapshot-1782006.tar.gz`
Alex M: routing now fully shifted off node-17. verify traffic: 0% to node-17. latency for sunnyside looks stable ~7ms P50 (brief spike to 45ms during evict).
Victoria CSM: shared update to customer: "We've detected a GPU hardware error on one node in your dedicated pool. We're draining the node and shifting traffic; you may see brief latency spikes. We'll follow up when node replacement scheduled"
Julia (solutions): customer replied: "Thanks. We're seeing degraded throughput on some batch jobs, please advise ETA."
Sara (oncall): hardware replacement ETA TBD — I'll engage infra for prioritization. tagging @Lee Infra for replacement scheduling.
Lee Infra: acknowledged. we've opened a replacement crew ticket; ETA on-site replacement 3 hours. meanwhile, we can attempt live migration to spare nodes in the same rack if thermal/power constraints allow.
Mike SRE: note — pool currently at 85% capacity. to avoid further customer impact we can: 1) burst to reserved spare capacity (if pool allowed), 2) offer temporary hosted fallback for customer (requires CSM opt-in).
Ben (prod): what's the cost/approval for a hosted fallback?
Victoria CSM: i can offer temporary hosted fallback for 2 days; will need exec approval but customer prefers continuity. i'll confirm acceptance.
Julia (solutions): if they accept, we'll need to provision model variant on hosted with same weights; estimate 20-30min for packaging and warm-up to acceptable latency.
Sara (oncall): for immediate mitigation, we already freed capacity by scaling other replicas. impact now limited to batch jobs that hit capacity peaks. monitoring queue backlog decreasing.
OpsBot: INCIDENT NOTE: node gpu-node-17 drained at 1782007099; evictions successful. hardware ticket hw-replace-7782 created by Lee Infra.
Victoria CSM: customer accepted hosted fallback. Julia, can your team start packaging?
Julia (solutions): starting containerize + push to hosted registry. `build: sunnyside-ggml-v2:hosted-1782007`
Alex M: routing config ready to split traffic 80% dedicated / 20% hosted once warm. will coordinate cutover window with Sara.
Sara (oncall): handing off to night oncall @Mike SRE — I'll add runbook notes and current state. handing over at 1782007500.
Mike SRE: taking over. notes: node-17 drained; replacement ETA 3h; hosted fallback accepted and build in progress; pool at 78% utilization; watch for NVMe IO errors on 16/18.
Ben (prod): postmortem action items: better spare capacity alarms for dedicated pools, auto-fallback opt-in workflow, cache snapshot before drain.
Victoria CSM: I'll coordinate proactive customer communication and SLA credit discussion if needed.
Lee Infra: scheduling RMA for node-17; will report arrival and replacement steps in this thread.
OpsBot: REMINDER: create incident ticket in JIRA: RED-INF-9654 and attach kernel oops logs from gpu-node-17.
Sara (oncall): thanks team. leaving thread open for replacement updates. :v:
Mike SRE: monitoring—no new errors after migration; batch backlog cleared in 18 minutes. keeping watch. :eyes:
